statements.text: Twelve lunar months total about 354 days, which is shorter than the roughly 365-day seasonal cycle.
Because the lunar year is shorter, the same lunar month drifts earlier relative to the seasons in later years.
A purely lunar calendar keeps each lunar month locked to the same season every year because months are still based on Moon phases.

stem:
Mehak's family uses a purely lunar calendar. Each month starts with a new Moon. Twelve lunar months make about 354 days. Seasons on Earth repeat in about 365 days. A harvest day fixed to one lunar month falls earlier in the seasonal year after a few years.

Which statements correctly explain why the lunar months do not stay aligned with the same seasons?

teacher.key_rationale: A lunar year of about 354 days is shorter than the seasonal year, so lunar months drift relative to seasons. Statement 3 wrongly claims they stay locked.
